subject: Consolidation of Q2-Q4 commits + optional capacity windows
messages:
From: Claire Huang <claire.huang@novacorp.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Cc: Ethan Morales <ethan.morales@novacorp.com>, procurement@novacorp.com
Date: Tue, 5 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal timeline + possible consolidation of three regional commits

Hi Dylan,

Quick note as we're starting renewal planning for the year: NovaCorp has three existing Redwood commitments across NA/EU/APAC that are on offset terms (Mar, Jul, Dec). We'd like to explore consolidating into a single annual contract to simplify billing and forecasting. Primary asks: 1) can we co-term into a single 12-month window starting 2027-04-01, 2) add optional capacity windows for Q2 and Q4 (burstable slots that we can draw against), and 3) a simple mechanism to increase committed units mid-term without penalty (we expect a stepped ramp).

Procurement asked for an initial sketch of pricing and whether co-terming triggers any penalties or true-up clauses. Attaching our internal draft schedule (spreadsheet). Can someone on your team lay out how Redwood typically handles staged ramping + optional burst capacity and whether auto-renew language needs to change?

Thanks,
Claire
Claire Huang
Director of Platform Engineering
NovaCorp

[attachment: Novacorp_proposed_schedule_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: dylan_brooks@redwood.com <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Claire Huang <claire.huang@novacorp.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 6 Jan 2027 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal timeline + possible consolidation of three regional commits

Hi Claire — thanks for the clear summary and the schedule. Happy to run this through and propose an option that balances forecast simplicity with cost predictability. High-level answers up front:

- Co-terming: yes, we can consolidate your three contracts into a single 12-month commitment effective 2027-04-01. We typically prorate remaining days on shorter terms into the new co-term to avoid double-billing.
- Staged ramping: we support a stepped commit schedule (e.g., 30% commit Apr-June, 60% Jul-Sep, 100% Oct-Dec) with true-up checkpoints quarterly. Unit pricing tiers can be blended or locked at signing — we can show both.
- Optional burst windows: we offer "burst credits" that are billed at a pre-agreed overage rate and can be attached as capacity buckets; these do not require expanding the committed baseline unless you convert them to a permanent increase.
- Mid-term increases: we can add a simple amendment process that lets you increase the committed capacity at any quarter start; the price for incremental units can be either the original committed price or a separate incremental price (we'll show both).

Looping in Marissa (our renewals lead) and Neha (sales ops) who'll assemble a formal co-term proposal and a draft amendment with the auto-renew wording. Would you prefer a one-pager commercial summary before we produce legal language?

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Renewals
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Claire Huang <claire.huang@novacorp.com>, dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 08:27:00 -0800
Subject: Draft commercial terms for consolidation + two optional models attached

Claire — attaching two clean options for your review:

Option A — Single annual co-term (simplest):
- Start: 2027-04-01; Term: 12 months
- Baseline commit: aggregated across NA/EU/APAC (sheet: blended baseline)
- Ramp schedule: Apr-Jun 30% baseline, Jul-Sep 60%, Oct-Mar 100% (note: sample ramp uses March quarter-end alignment)
- Burst credits: 500k tokens per quarter at an overage rate of $0.0025/token
- True-up: quarterly; overage billed monthly; unused baseline does not credit back
- Pricing: 8% discount vs list if signed at co-term

Option B — Phased multi-year (cost smoothing + protected incremental price):
- 24-month agreement with committed annual minimums and per-quarter step-ups
- Lower incremental price for mid-term capacity increases (protects against market rate shifts)
- Early termination limited to business-critical carve-outs

Attached: redwood_co-term_models_Q1-2027.pdf and an editable amendment template (we removed confidential legalese). Highlights and questions are inline in the PDF.

If this looks directionally right, we can convert Option A into a short commercial exhibit and route to legal. A couple of procurement items we'll need you to confirm: trademarked billing entity, PO cadence, and whether NovaCorp requires a dedicated SLA for peak periods (we can offer a Premium SLA for guaranteed latency during scheduled bursts).

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Renewals Manager, Redwood Inference
[attachment: redwood_co-term_models_Q1-2027.pdf]

From: Claire Huang <claire.huang@novacorp.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Cc: Ethan Morales <ethan.morales@novacorp.com>, procurement@novacorp.com
Date: Thu, 21 Jan 2027 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft commercial terms for consolidation + two optional models attached

Thanks Marissa — Option A is close to what we want. A few clarifying items from procurement/legal: 

1) Auto-renew: we need a 30-day opt-out notice before renewal rather than automatic renewal without notice. Is that acceptable?
2) Burst credits: we prefer burst credits to be purchasable at the start of the quarter (to align with internal approvals) and refundable (prorated) if not consumed within that quarter.
3) True-up timing: can true-ups be performed on net usage across regions (so we don’t double true-up local spikes)?

Also, our finance team asked whether co-terming the three existing PO numbers into one would require separate invoices for each original PO (they'd like separate invoices, one per existing PO, even if the commercial contract is consolidated).

If we can get a short amendment that addresses these three points, procurement can sign off quickly. Happy to hop on a 30-minute call if easier.

— Claire

From: dylan_brooks@redwood.com <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Claire Huang <claire.huang@novacorp.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft commercial terms for consolidation + two optional models attached

Claire — thanks for the feedback and the clear list. Marissa and I reviewed with Sales Ops and Legal; attached is a redline that captures the agreed mechanics. Quick answers inline: 

1) Auto-renew: we can change to a 30-day opt-out window prior to renewal; we'll reflect that in the contract exhibit.
2) Burst credits: we can make burst buckets purchasable at quarter start and support prorated refunds for unused, up to a defined cap (we included a 25% administrative fee on refunds in the draft — happy to discuss). If you'd rather we hold burst credit reservations without prepayment, that is also possible but we'd reserve capacity and apply a reservation fee.
3) True-up: yes — we'll calculate true-ups on consolidated net usage across regions to avoid double true-ups on localized spikes.

Invoices: we can emit separate invoices tied to your original PO numbers while keeping a single master commercial agreement. We'll add an invoice exhibit specifying PO mapping rules.

Next steps: 1) Please confirm you want Option A (single co-term starting 2027-04-01) and the refund mechanics for burst credits; 2) we will send the final commercial exhibit and the redlined contract for signature the following week.

Attaching: redwood-co-term-draft-2027-02-20.pdf (redline)

Best regards,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Renewals
Redwood Inference
[attachment: redwood-co-term-draft-2027-02-20.pdf]
